task_context.reference_solution:
The desired area is the infinite series $\frac{4}{9}\left(1+\frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{9^2}+\cdots\right).$

Simplifying, we have $\frac{4}{9}\left( \frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{9}}\right)=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}.$

Fine. I'll do it. In the first step, 4/9 is shaded. Then we take the center square (which is 1/9 of the total) and shade 4/9 of that. So that's (4/9) * (1/9). Then we take the new center square and do it again. This looks like a geometric series. Am I on the right track?

That is exactly the right approach. You've identified that the shaded area is the sum of a geometric series. Can you write out the first few terms of this series and identify the first term (a) and the common ratio (r)?

The terms are 4/9, (4/9)(1/9), (4/9)(1/9)^2... so a = 4/9 and r = 1/9. I know the formula for an infinite sum is S = a / (1 - r). If I plug these in, I get the answer. Just tell me if my a and r are correct so I can stop wasting time.

Your identification of the first term and the common ratio is correct. You have all the components needed to find the total shaded area using the sum formula. Go ahead and perform that final calculation!
